transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: Tue Nov 10 2026 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Michael Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neill (Velora PM), Sara Gomez (Velora SRE), Rajesh Kumar (Velora CTO)
Links shared: pilot-run-results-2026-11-09.xlsx, /redwood/pilot/velora/latency-heatmap.png, security-brief-v2.pdf

Summary:
Quick review of the week-one pilot metrics, focus on choosing model/variant to pin for public traffic, and agree emergency "rollforward" playbook (not just rollbacks). Action items around running large-scale latency/cost runs and a drill.

Topics covered:
- Model quality vs cost tradeoffs (3B vs 7B vs 13B variants)
- Version pinning semantics and compatibility matrix
- Soft fallback / shadowing and emergency rollforward strategy
- Observability gaps (token-level billing, KV cache hits)

Action items (echoed in metadata) and next steps at end.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Michael: okay hi everyone thanks for joining, um this is Michael from Redwood, I'm the AE on the Velora pilot. We have Priya from SE with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Liam: good morning yeah thanks Michael, doing well. Quick note, Rajesh is jumping on for the second half, he has a customer call now.
[00:12] Michael: perfect. We'll run the agenda quick: results review, model pick for traffic pin, and then emergency rollforward plan. Priya will lead perf details.
[00:20] Priya: hey all, thanks. I'll start with the summary of the run we did yesterday - we executed the 10k request synthetic workload across the three candidate model variants: redwood-ema-3b, redwood-7b-cpu-friendly, and redwood-13b-opt. We collected p50/p95 latencies, cost per 1k tokens, and quality metrics from the eval set you shared.
[00:39] Priya: notes - p50 for 3b was 75ms per token (GPU inference), p95 200ms; 7b p50 110ms p95 320ms; 13b p50 210ms p95 680ms, rough numbers but consistent across runs. The KV cache hit rate for repeat prefixes was about 14% in our synthetic - your real traffic had higher prefix reuse so expect better in production.
[01:02] Sara: sorry can I interrupt, when you say per token is that end-to-end or just model token generation? We need p95 end-to-end including network and our proxy.
[01:10] Priya: good catch - those are service-side generation times only. We added an example e2e run from our staging egress through your proxy and it added ~45-60ms median depending on region. So if you budget for e2e p95 for 7b that's roughly 380-450ms in us-west.
[01:26] Liam: and cost delta between 7b and 13b? We need the delta to estimate monthly run rates.
[01:31] Priya: in our run cost-per-1k-tokens (approx): 3b=$0.18, 7b=$0.45, 13b=$1.20. The biggest savings is when you can leverage caching/shadowing to avoid hot paths. Also quantized 8-bit runs for 7b reduce cost ~30% with small latency hit.
[01:50] Rajesh: (joins) hey team, apologies. I caught the tail of that - can we back up - what's the quality delta you mentioned? If we pick 7b pinning, do we expect more hallucinations versus 13b?
[02:00] Michael: good question. Liam, do you want to recap the eval pass?
[02:04] Liam: sure. We did the 1k-sample human eval on the customer prompts. Counted answer accuracy on the structured task and flagged hallucination instances. 13b had 4% hallucination, 7b ~7.5%, 3b ~12%. There are also answer-length differences, 13b is more verbose. Our acceptance threshold was <=8% hallucination and >=92% task accuracy. 7b just squeaks by on accuracy but is borderline on hallucination in edge cases.
[02:32] Priya: that maps with our automated eval. We also ran a reranker pairing where outputs from 7b got reranked by a small 1b verifier model; that reduced hallucination to ~3.5% but adds ~40ms. So tradeoff: extra compute (and cost) for quality.
[02:48] Sara: do we have an RBAC or SSO concern if we change pinned version during business hours? We have strict audit log needs.
[02:55] Michael: yes - we mapped that. Redwood's rollout is API-level pinning; version changes are auditable in the control plane. We can gate changes via an approval step that requires two approvals from your side (PM + SRE) before a live pin change. All changes produce audit logs and can be exportable to your SIEM.
[03:14] Rajesh: good. Now on the emergency strategy — our concern is that rollback takes time and sometimes causes double-faults. What do you mean by "rollforward"?
[03:21] Priya: yeah we wanted to introduce 'rollforward' as an ops concept: instead of reverting to an older model, we pivot traffic to a lighter variant or a read-only cached response path while we warm or hot-swap a new compatible version. It's effectively a circuit-breaker plus fallback that prefers availability over fidelity if the active variant starts failing or latency spikes.
[03:39] Liam: so example: we have 7b pinned and it starts returning degraded quality; you propose routing 20% to 13b and 80% to a cached response or 'safe' retriever?
[03:47] Priya: exactly. We also support 'dark traffic' or shadowing where a candidate 13b gets shadowed behind 7b without affecting e2e latency. That gives you real-world quality signals before you flip pins.
[03:58] Sara: what's the cost exposure for that? Shadowing doubles inference calls which doubles cost temporarily correct?
[04:04] Priya: yes, shadowing increases compute cost. We suggested limited sampling (2-5% traffic) for ongoing shadowing. For emergency rollforward we can selectively send to a pre-warmed pool of cheaper quantized 7b or to a canned retrieval path that has near-zero compute. That keeps cost bounded.
[04:22] Liam: can we have a policy: if p95 > 500ms for two consecutive 5-minute windows, we auto-shift to rollforward target?
[04:29] Priya: yes alerting and autoswitch policies are configurable. You can set thresholds on latency, error-rate, or quality metric regressions.
[04:35] Rajesh: I want to ensure compatibility — are models interchangeable across our prompt templates? We've seen tokenization differences previously.
[04:43] Priya: great point — we ran the compat matrix. Most prompts are fine, but two prompts that rely on HTML sanitization behave differently on 3b because of length truncation and tokenization. We documented exact prompt token deltas in the sheet. If you pin 7b we recommend a small prompt shim on the client side for those two endpoints.
[04:58] Michael: note on pinning: Redwood supports model version constraints. You can pin to exact model hash, or to a model family with allowed minor-version roll-forward, or to 'floating' with safety gates. For Velora's pilot we recommended 'family pin with floor', meaning allow patch upgrades unless they change decoding or tokenization semantics.
[05:18] Liam: hmm we prefer deterministic behavior - I'd rather pin to exact artifact for the pilot then loosen later.
[05:24] Rajesh: agree, for compliance initial pin to exact artifact hash. How big is the artifact? If we need to rollforward to 13b do we need to pre-pull weights?
[05:32] Priya: for production rollforward to 13b, you want a warm pool. Pre-pulling weights and keeping a small warm pool reduces cold start from minutes to sub-30s. We can manage warm pools in Redwood Dedicated or Private.
[05:44] Sara: can Redwood pre-warm a quantized 7b as the primary fallback so we don't need to keep the expensive 13b warm all the time?
[05:51] Priya: yes that's the recommended cost-savvy plan. Quantized 7b warms fast and acts as emergency stand-in; 13b is only for targeted traffic if quality thresholds need it.
[05:59] Michael: quick interjection - we noticed a spike in the KV cache miss rate in the 10am-11am run. Sara, can you confirm any upstream proxy churn?
[06:06] Sara: we had a rolling deploy on our edge last night, there may be session affinity resets. We'll correlate.
[06:12] Priya: that explains it; cache warming helps a lot. We'll include recommendations for sticky routing and prefix-aware cache priming in the runbook.
[06:20] Liam: let's talk about the control-plane ops for emergency drills. We want a rehearsed drill where we simulate the 7b degrading and exercise the rollforward to quantized 7b, then to warm 13b if needed.
[06:30] Michael: propose this drill: 1) trigger at 11am PT on a low-traffic day; 2) alert threshold breach sim; 3) auto-shift to quantized fallback; 4) validate end-to-end for 30 minutes; 5) scale up 13b and switch 10% traffic to verify quality; 6) rollback to normal. We'll own steps 3 and 5 via pilot control plane.
[06:52] Rajesh: timeline? I'd like this by next Friday (2026-11-20).
[06:56] Michael: ok we'll plan the drill for 2026-11-20. Priya will run preparatory tests.
[07:00] Priya: action - I'll run a set of readiness tests and share a checklist by Friday. Also will run the 50k-message perf run to validate cost numbers.
[07:08] Liam: any security concerns with shadowing to 3rd-party? We need to ensure no PHI or PII leaves Velora.
[07:15] Michael: good call — we configured the pilot to use Private mode for the PII endpoints. For the public endpoints we can use hosted with strong redaction. We will also share our SOC2 and ISO docs, and the updated dataflow diagram.
[07:28] Sara: can you also share the audit log format? We need to ingest into Splunk.
[07:32] Michael: yes I'll include sample audit export and a Splunk ingestion example.
[07:36] Liam: on the model pinning UI — any way to preview the impact of a pin change before committing?
[07:41] Priya: in Redwood Console we have a 'dry-run' toggle that simulates routing and shows expected latency/cost delta using historical telemetry. It won't change live traffic but gives an estimate.
[07:52] Rajesh: good. Also please add an approval gate in the dry-run results so we can do a two-person approve.
[07:58] Michael: noted. We'll add a mandatory two-approver step for production pin changes during business hours.
[08:03] Liam: ok I'm leaning toward pinning exact 7b artifact for the pilot but enabling the emergency rollforward to quantized 7b. If after shadowing 13b for 2 weeks quality improves we can promote. Does that sound right?
[08:14] Rajesh: yes, but add the drill we discussed.
[08:17] Michael: perfect. Quick recap of action items: Priya - perf runs and readiness checklist; Michael - pricing + catalog spreadsheet + audit log sample; Sara - validate egress and firewall rules; Liam - confirm approved drill window with product calendar.
[08:33] Priya: small note: we found two prompts that need client shim to normalize tokens. I'll put the exact transform snippet in the sheet.
[08:41] Liam: thanks.
[08:44] Michael: any other questions?
[08:46] Rajesh: one last - if we need to do a fast fix we prefer rollforward to a previously shadowed 13b variant rather than rollback. Can you ensure the shadowed variants are automatically warmed on detection?
[08:56] Priya: we can automate pre-warming when shadowing coverage exceeds X% or when the drift score rises. We'll include the policy in the runbook options.
[09:05] Sara: thanks. That helps.
[09:08] Michael: ok we'll follow up in email with the files, and schedule the drill. Thanks everyone.
[09:13] Liam: thanks y'all.
[09:15] End of meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: automatic transcription captured a few mis-heard acronyms (e.g., "K-V cash" instead of KV cache, "sam-el" for SAML in one mention) — validated by SE. There is occasional crosstalk and filler words which were left in to preserve conversational context.
